headline: Japanese Scientists Begin FIRST Human Trials of Drug That Regrows Missing Teeth
explanation: A team at Kyoto University and Kitano Hospital in Japan genuinely began human trials in 2024 of a drug that blocks the USAG-1 protein, which normally suppresses tooth regrowth. The researchers are aiming for public availability by around 2030. It sounds like science fiction, but it is peer-reviewed, on the clinical-trial registry, and widely reported in credible outlets.

headline: Instagram Rolling Out New Feature That Shows EXACTLY Who Views Your Profile the Most
explanation: Instagram has repeatedly and publicly stated that it does not — and will not — show users who views their profile. This rumor is one of the most recycled social-media hoaxes of the last decade and resurfaces every few months. Third-party apps that claim to reveal 'profile stalkers' typically steal login credentials or run scams.

headline: MrBeast Pays for 1,000 People's Eye Surgeries So They Can SEE for the First Time
explanation: In January 2023 Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast) released a video titled '1,000 Blind People See For The First Time' in which he funded cataract surgeries for exactly 1,000 people through a partnership with SEE International. The video was covered by mainstream news outlets and sparked public debate about whether philanthropy should be framed as entertainment — but the surgeries themselves are documented and real.

headline: Netflix Password Sharing Now Officially ILLEGAL in US — Users Can Be Fined Up to $500
explanation: Netflix did crack down on password sharing starting in 2023, charging an extra fee for accounts used across households. But that is a company policy, not a law. There is no US statute banning password sharing and no government-issued $500 fine. This claim blurs the line between what a private company can do and what the law requires — exactly the kind of wording misinformation exploits.
